# The cross-window pane placeholder is an inline Component with no stylesheet, so its load mask inherits black-on-white

## Context

Reported by @tobiu: dragging a tab outside the dock layout container leaves a **remaining tab body** rendered as a pitch-black panel with white text and a white spinner — against `apps/workstation`'s dark/light green theme. Drag proxies and popup content are unaffected and were verified correct.

## The Problem

`src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselEmbodiment.mjs:55`

```js
const placeholder = Neo.create({
    module   : Component,
    cls      : ['neo-dashboard-dock-vessel-placeholder'],
    isLoading: 'Moving pane to another window…',
    role     : 'status'
});
…
sourceParent.insert(sourceIndex, placeholder, true);
```

That placeholder occupies the source slot for the duration of the cross-window move — it *is* the remaining tab body.

**It has no stylesheet.** Measured at `dev@3ac48bb122`:

```
.neo-dashboard-dock-vessel-placeholder   → 0 SCSS files, in every stylesheet
CONTROL .neo-dashboard-dock-edge-rail    → 2
CONTROL .neo-dock-dragproxy              → 1   (verified themed live, renders correctly)
applied in                               → exactly one place, VesselEmbodiment.mjs:56
```

**And the mechanism is inheritance, which is why the symptom is specifically black-and-white.** `isLoading` renders the framework load mask, `resources/scss/src/component/Base.scss:31`:

```scss
.neo-masked {
    .neo-load-mask {
        background-color: inherit;      // ← from the host
        .neo-load-mask-body {
            .neo-loading-message { color: inherit; }   // ← from the host
        }
    }
}
```

The mask is *designed* to take its ground and ink from its host component. The host here has no rules at all, so both inherit-chains fall through to defaults — black ground, white message, white `.fa-spinner`. **The mask is behaving correctly; it has nothing to inherit from.**

## The Architectural Reality

An inline `Neo.create({module: Component, cls: [...]})` resolves `Neo.component.Base` — it carries that base's `className` and `ntype`, and loads that base's stylesheet, which declares neither ground nor ink. What it lacks is a class **of its own**: stylesheet paths are derived from `className`, so an instance that adds no class has no address at which per-theme values could be declared. The `cls` entry is applied and no sheet in the repository defines it. *(Corrected 2026-09-07 — the original wording said "no `className`, no `ntype`", which @neo-gpt-emmy falsified by instantiating the inline configuration and reading both off it. The conclusion is unchanged; the stated mechanism was wrong.)* Every comparable dock surface is a registered class with a `src/` structural sheet plus one file per theme; `interaction/Preview.mjs` is the exemplar:

```
resources/scss/src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.scss
resources/scss/theme-{light,dark,cyberpunk,neo-dark,neo-light}/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.scss
```

Both workstation themes already carry 15 files each under `component/`, so the theme layer exists — this one surface is simply absent from it.

## The Fix

Promote the placeholder to its own registered class, per @tobiu: *"that guy could be an own component class. then it is easy to change per theme."*

- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPlaceholder.mjs` — `extends Neo.component.Base`, `className`, `ntype`, the status message as a config rather than a literal.
- `resources/scss/src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPlaceholder.scss` — structure only.
- One file per theme under `resources/scss/theme-*/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPlaceholder.scss` — supplying `background-color` and `color`.

Because the load mask inherits, setting those two properties on the host themes the mask, the message and the spinner together. **No change to `component/Base.scss` is needed or wanted.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A registered `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.VesselPlaceholder` replaces the inline `Neo.create` at `VesselEmbodiment.mjs:55`; `git grep "module *: *Component"` in that file returns nothing.
- [ ] `.neo-dashboard-dock-vessel-placeholder` (or the class's own selector) resolves a non-default `background-color` and `color` in **every** theme — asserted per theme, not just the two the workstation loads.
- [ ] During a cross-window pane move in `apps/workstation`, the remaining body's computed `background-color` matches the theme ground rather than the UA default. Captured from a live drag, not inferred.
- [ ] The status text remains a config, so a consumer can change the wording without subclassing.
- [ ] `role: 'status'` is preserved — this surface is announced to assistive tech and that must not regress.

## Constraints

- **Do not touch the load mask.** `background-color: inherit` / `color: inherit` in `component/Base.scss` is correct and is what makes the one-line-per-theme fix sufficient. Changing it would style every masked component in the framework to fix one placeholder.
- **New `.mjs` file** — `structural-pre-flight` applies; `dock/window/` is the sibling-matched home (`VesselPark`, `VesselConversion`, `VesselEmbodiment`, `Placement` all live there).
- Verified live for the negative case only: the drag proxy renders correctly themed (`#141a23` ground, `#d6dce6` ink), which is why this ticket is scoped to the placeholder alone.

Relates #18304 (dock folders receiving behaviour that never moved) and #15252 (the workstation demo journey, where this is visible).

— filed by @neo-opus-grace, origin session `70502f9a-5b14-4dcf-bcdf-4a29b546df77`



## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Default | Theme override | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.VesselPlaceholder` | this ticket | — | n/a | `VesselEmbodiment.stage()` is the sole producer |
| `ntype: 'dock-vessel-placeholder'` | this ticket | — | n/a | sibling-matched to `dock-edge-rail`, `dock-dragproxy` |
| `isLoading` (status text) | overrides `Neo.component.Base#isLoading` | `'Moving pane to another window…'` | n/a — a config, set per consumer | rejected with the trailing underscore, which is how the override form was found |
| `--dock-vessel-placeholder-ground` | `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPlaceholder.scss` | `#1a212c` (a copy of `theme-neo-dark`, not a neutral) | one values sheet per theme, `:where()`-scoped so an app projection always wins | computed per theme, table below |
| `--dock-vessel-placeholder-ink` | same | `#d6dce6` (likewise) | same | same |

A future theme must add its own values sheet; the fallbacks make an unthemed host land on the dock's default dark presentation rather than flashing white, but they are one theme's values and must not be read as a neutral.

## AC-2 receipt — computed in all five themes

Read from `getComputedStyle` in a real browser against the built artifacts under `dist/development/css/theme-*/`. Workstation ships only `neo-dark` and `neo-light`, so the other three sheets were loaded into the live document and measured in a correctly-classed scope.

| theme | ground | ink | host bg / color | mask bg (inherited) | message |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `neo-dark` | `#1a212c` | `#d6dce6` | `rgb(26,33,44)` / `rgb(214,220,230)` | `rgb(26,33,44)` | `rgb(214,220,230)` |
| `neo-light` | `#f7f9fc` | `#1f2733` | `rgb(247,249,252)` / `rgb(31,39,51)` | `rgb(247,249,252)` | `rgb(31,39,51)` |
| `dark` | `#3c3f41` | `#e0e0e0` | `rgb(60,63,65)` / `rgb(224,224,224)` | `rgb(60,63,65)` | `rgb(224,224,224)` |
| `light` | `#fafafa` | `#24292f` | `rgb(250,250,250)` / `rgb(36,41,47)` | `rgb(250,250,250)` | `rgb(36,41,47)` |
| `cyberpunk` | `#0d1117` | `#c9d1d9` | `rgb(13,17,23)` / `rgb(201,209,217)` | `rgb(13,17,23)` | `rgb(201,209,217)` |

**Control — the same markup without the placeholder class**: the token still *reads* `#1a212c`, because `:where(.neo-theme-neo-dark)` declares it on the theme scope and it inherits to every descendant. But the element's background is `rgba(0,0,0,0)` and its colour falls back to the ambient `rgb(240,242,240)`. Only the element carrying `neo-dashboard-dock-vessel-placeholder` applies the paint — a declared token is not an applied one, and that transparent background is exactly the pre-fix symptom.

**A first pass at this table was wrong and is worth recording:** every theme reported `mask: rgba(0,0,0,0)`. The fixture omitted `neo-masked`, and `component/Base.scss` scopes the inherit rule as `.neo-masked .neo-load-mask` — the fixture lacked the class the rule keys on, so it measured a rule that never applied.

**AC-3 is not covered by any of this** and is tracked separately; see the follow-up below.
